questions.question: According to Article 1 of Law 65-00, what fundamental principle does compulsory health insurance rely on?
options: The contributory principle and risk pooling
The principle of social assistance and national solidarity
The principle of total free care for all
The principle of medical selection and prevention
questions.explanation: AMO is based on the contributory principle and risk pooling.

questions.question: According to Article 2, to which categories of persons does the basic compulsory health insurance apply?
options: Civil servants, employees, pensioners, self-employed workers, and students
Only private sector employees and their dependents
Exclusively state and local government civil servants
Only pension holders from public and private sectors
questions.explanation: AMO applies to all these categories: civil servants, employees, pensioners, self-employed, liberal professionals, students, and former resistance members.

questions.question: According to Article 3, who is the medical assistance scheme (RAMED) intended for?
options: Economically disadvantaged persons not subject to AMO
Active civil servants and state agents
Self-employed workers in liberal professions
Students in public higher education
questions.explanation: RAMED is intended for economically disadvantaged persons who do not benefit from any AMO scheme.

questions.question: According to Article 5, who are the dependents covered by compulsory health insurance?
options: The spouse, children under 21, and disabled children
The spouse only and first-degree parents
Children up to 18 and dependent grandchildren
All ascendants and descendants without age limit
questions.explanation: Article 5 defines dependents as: the spouse, children under 21 (26 for students), and disabled children without age limit.

questions.question: According to Article 5, up to what age is an unmarried child pursuing higher education covered?
options: Up to 26 years upon proof of studies
Up to 21 years without specific condition
Up to 30 years for higher education
Until degree completion without age limit
questions.explanation: The age limit is extended to 26 for unmarried children pursuing higher education, upon justification.

questions.question: According to Article 5, can the insured person request extension of AMO benefits to their parents?
options: Yes, provided they pay their contribution
No, parents are never covered by AMO
Yes, automatically without additional contribution
Yes, only if parents are over 70
questions.explanation: The insured person may request extension to their father and mother, provided they pay their contribution.

questions.question: According to Article 7, what types of care are guaranteed by compulsory health insurance?
options: Curative, preventive, rehabilitation, maternity, and dental care
Only curative care and hospitalization
Aesthetic care and spa treatments
Exclusively medications and biological analyses
questions.explanation: Article 7 lists: preventive, curative, rehabilitation, maternity, dental, orthodontics for children, etc.

questions.question: According to Article 8, which benefits are excluded from the scope of compulsory health insurance?
options: Aesthetic surgery and alternative medicine
Reconstructive surgery and implants
Dental care and orthodontics
Medical biology analyses and radiology
questions.explanation: Article 8 excludes: aesthetic surgery, spa treatments, acupuncture, mesotherapy, thalassotherapy, homeopathy, and alternative medicine.

questions.question: According to Article 9, what is the rule regarding the portion remaining at the insured person's expense?
options: The insured person remains free to take out complementary insurance
The insured person cannot take out complementary insurance
The remaining portion is always covered by the State
The ticket modérateur is prohibited by law
questions.explanation: Article 9 specifies that the insured person remains free to take out complementary insurance.

questions.question: According to Article 9, what does the law provide in case of serious or disabling illness?
options: Total or partial exemption from the ticket modérateur
An increase in the insured person's contribution rate
Automatic exclusion from the insurance scheme
A lump-sum reimbursement without conditions
questions.explanation: In case of serious or disabling illness requiring long-term care, the remaining portion is exempted totally or partially.

questions.question: According to Article 10, in what form can certain items such as devices be reimbursed?
options: In the form of a lump sum defined by regulation
In the form of full reimbursement without limit
Only in the form of per-procedure reimbursement
In the form of variable reimbursement depending on the patient
questions.explanation: Article 10 specifies that certain items, particularly devices and medical equipment, are reimbursed as a lump sum.

questions.question: According to Article 11, what are the reimbursement methods provided for by law?
options: Per procedure, by pathology, by global allocation, or by capitation
Only per procedure upon presentation of invoices
Exclusively by lump sum per homogeneous disease group
Only by capitation with a referring physician
questions.explanation: Article 11 provides for: per-procedure reimbursement, lump sum by pathology, global allocation, prepayment, or capitation.

questions.question: According to Article 13, can benefits be reimbursed if provided abroad?
options: Yes, in case of unexpected illness or lack of appropriate care in Morocco
No, only benefits provided within the national territory are reimbursable
Yes, automatically without any prior condition
Yes, only if the patient is on a business trip
questions.explanation: Benefits abroad are admitted in case of unexpected illness during a stay, or when care cannot be provided in Morocco, with prior agreement.

questions.question: According to Article 14, what fundamental right does the AMO beneficiary retain?
options: Free choice of practitioner and healthcare establishment
Obligation to consult the designated attending physician
The right to choose only in the public sector
The prohibition to change attending physician
questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees the beneficiary free choice of practitioner, healthcare establishment, pharmacist, and paramedical professional.

questions.question: According to Article 18, who conducts the negotiations for national agreements?
options: The National Health Insurance Agency (ANAM)
The Ministry of Health directly
The managing bodies alone
The Competition Council
questions.explanation: Agreements are concluded at the initiative and under the leadership of ANAM.

questions.question: According to Article 19, with whom are national agreements concluded for the private sector?
options: With the national councils of professional orders
With patient unions
With private insurance companies
With the Central Bank of Morocco
questions.explanation: Agreements are concluded between the managing bodies and the national councils of the relevant professional orders.

questions.question: According to Article 24, what sanctions can be imposed on a provider for non-compliance with the agreement?
options: Removal from the agreement for a determined period
A flat fine of 10,000 dirhams
Definitive suspension of their professional practice
A simple warning without consequences
questions.explanation: ANAM may decide to place a provider outside the agreement for non-compliance with the terms of the agreement.

questions.question: According to Article 26, what is the purpose of the medical control exercised by the managing bodies?
options: Verify the conformity of prescriptions and identify abuses
Control the quality of the practice's equipment
Verify the number of patients treated per day
Control the bank accounts of providers
questions.explanation: The control aims to verify the conformity of prescriptions, the validity of benefits, and to identify abuses and fraud.

questions.question: According to Article 32, to what condition is the opening of entitlement to benefits subject?
options: Prior payment of contributions due
Approval by a consulting physician
Prior agreement of the Ministry of Health
An automatic six-month waiting period
questions.explanation: The opening of entitlement is subject to prior payment of contributions.

questions.question: According to Article 34, how long does a person retain their rights after ceasing to meet the conditions?
options: A maximum period of six months
A period of two full years
A period of only one month
No period of rights retention
questions.explanation: Persons who cease to meet the conditions benefit from the retention of their rights for a maximum period of six months.

questions.question: According to Article 35, for how long do the dependents of a deceased insured person continue to receive benefits?
options: For a period of two years
For a period of six months
For a period of five years
Until the end of the dependents' lives
questions.explanation: The dependents of the deceased insured person continue to receive benefits for a period of two years.

questions.question: According to Article 44, what is prohibited for AMO managing bodies?
options: Combining insurance management with the management of healthcare establishments
Exercising medical control over providers
Concluding agreements with healthcare professionals
Collecting contributions from employers
questions.explanation: Managing bodies cannot combine AMO management with the management of healthcare establishments or medical equipment supply.

questions.question: According to Article 130, what fine does an employer incur who fails to register?
options: A fine of 5,000 to 50,000 dirhams
A fine of 1,000 to 5,000 dirhams
A fine of 50,000 to 100,000 dirhams
A prison sentence of 6 months to 2 years
questions.explanation: Article 130 provides for a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 dirhams for the employer who fails to register.

questions.question: According to Article 131, what is the penalty for non-registration of an employee?
options: A fine of 1,000 dirhams for each employee concerned
A flat fine of 5,000 dirhams
A suspension of the right to recruit
A prison sentence of 3 months to 1 year
questions.explanation: Article 131 provides for a fine of 1,000 dirhams for each unregistered employee.

questions.question: According to Article 135, what is punished by a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 dirhams?
options: Fraud or false declaration to obtain undue benefits
Refusal of medical control by a provider
Non-payment of contributions by the employer
Risk selection by a managing body
questions.explanation: Article 135 punishes fraud or false declaration to obtain undue benefits.
